occurrenceRemarks: Coromandel Ilisha / Jeweled Shad / (Ilisha filigera) Recorded from Barguna district, Bangladesh. Introduction: A moderately slender pristigasterid shad with a large eye, projecting lower jaw, 34–38 belly scutes (23–26 pre-pelvic + 11–13 post-pelvic). Dorsal origin around mid-body; anal origin below dorsal base. Common names include Jeweled/Jewe[l]led Shad, Coromandel ilisha; in Bangladesh: Boro Choukka / Choukka mach / Faissa. Global range: Indo-West Pacific. Documented from the Indian Ocean (Mumbai to India’s east coast; possibly Andaman Sea) and parts of the South China Sea (NW Borneo—Sarawak/Kalimantan). Bangladesh records (literature): — Upper Bay of Bengal off the Bangladesh coast, based on set-bag-net catches with detailed growth/recruitment analyses. — Southeast coast landings (Chattogram & Cox’s Bazar) studied 2013–2014; also noted as occurring from Indian coast to New Guinea and to the South China Sea. — Listed in national marine fish checklists/portals and field references for Bangladesh. This Barguna record adds a confirmed occurrence from the SW coast of Bangladesh; published work has focused more on the upper and SE Bay of Bengal. Availability of the species in fish nets and local markets of Barguna, and Pirojpur district is almost regular in monsoon but not in large amount. Maybe roam in small flock. Habitat & depth. Coastal marine and lower estuaries; tolerates broad salinity (reported ~5–38 ppt). Typically pelagic-neritic, recorded from ~0–50 m depth. Breeding / recruitment (Bangladesh data). In the upper Bay of Bengal off Bangladesh, two recruitment pulses were detected: August–October and March–May, based on length-frequency analyses of set-bag-net catches. (Recruitment timing implies spawning preceding these peaks.) Availability & fishery notes (Bangladesh). Caught by trawls, estuarine and marine set-bag nets, and beach seines. Historic trawl surveys (1984–86) attributed ~0.44% of demersal fish catch to this species; studies in 2013–2014 indicated the stock on the SE coast was not over-exploited at that time. Marketed locally and described as having high market price. Conservation status. — Global (IUCN Red List): Data Deficient (2017). — Bangladesh (National Red List 2015): Least Concern. Key references (open sources): • FishBase species summary for I. filigera (distribution, habitat, IUCN status). • Rashid et al. 2007. Growth, mortality & recruitment of I. filigera off Bangladesh (J-STAGE—full text; recruitment months). • Al-Mamun et al. 2019. SE coast of Bangladesh study (gears, habitat, price; SE landings). • Marine Biodiversity Portal of Bangladesh (local names, national occurrence & references). • IUCN Bangladesh Red List (national status).

occurrenceRemarks: Der Rotfeuerfisch (Pterois miles) ist im Roten Meer und im Indischen Ozean verbreitet. Als invasive Spezies kommt er auch an der nordamerikanischen Ostküste und in der Karibik vor. Er ist inzwischen auch durch den Suezkanal in das südöstliche Mittelmeer eingewandert (Lessepssche Migration). Die Art hat innerhalb eines Jahres fast die gesamte Südostküste von Zypern besiedelt (Stand 2016). Er dringt bis in eine Wassertiefe von 50 Meter vor. Nachts und in der Dämmerung jagt er nach Fischen (Quelle: Wikipedia)
